newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Clinton route at APEC switched in security alert.
newsitem.headline: Clinton route at APEC switched in security alert.

text.p: Philippine police made a last-minute switch on Saturday to U.S. President Bill Clinton's proposed route from Manila airport to the hotel he will stay at before Monday's APEC economic summit.
They made the switch after reports that two suspicious-looking men may have placed an object inside a traffic signal control box on the original route.
Police were still trying to open the control box while Clinton was being taken safely to the historic Manila Hotel.

A senior U.S. official has said Philippine police fear a leftist hit squad may attempt to mount an attack while Clinton and other leaders of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum are here for Monday's summit.

Police found explosives in the arrival area of Manila's international airport on Wednesday. They originally said the explosives had been planted during a security exercise but a leaked intelligence report later contradicted this.
There was no indication of who really planted the explosives.
Police guarding Clinton's route from the airport on Saturday decided to take no chances after witnesses reported seeing two suspicious-looking men open the traffic signal control box.
"I would rather be laughed at than put my country in an embarrassing position," the police colonel in charge of investigating the incident told a Reuters Television crew at the scene.

President Fidel Ramos has pledged to ensure the safety of the APEC leaders, their cabinet ministers and some 6,000 foreign delegates and journalists covering the fourth annual summit and ministerial conference that preceded it.
